'''Child of the Dragon''' is a name given to [[Da'shain Aiel]] by the people of the time of the [[War of Power|War of the Shadow]].

{{dablink|For the race called by the name see the page [[Aiel]]''. For the chapter in The Dragon Reborn, see ''[[The Dragon Reborn/Chapter 56|People of the Dragon]]''.}}

== First reference ==
At the [[Eye of the World]] when the [[Nym|Green Man]] first sees [[Rand al'Thor]] he calls him a Child of the Dragon.

{{quote|Strange clothes you wear, Child of the Dragon. Has the Wheel turned so far? Do the People of the Dragon return to the First Covenant? But you wear a sword. That is neither now nor then.{{ref/book|1|49}}}} 

When Rand asks him what does he mean, Someshta, touching his wounded head explains that his memories are torn and he himself is unsure.   

== Second reference ==
Rand, – in his [[Visions of Rhuidean|seventh vision]] in the [[Glass columns|glass forest ter'angreal of Rhuidean]], being [[Jonai]] the Da'shain Aiel, – meets [[Someshta]] in one of the room of the Hall of the Servants just before the Nym gets the task from the Aes Sedai to guard the [[Eye of the World]]. Someshta's head is wounded, he has lost part of his memories, he doesn't recognise Jonai. The Aiel sadly tells him they are friends since his childhood. The Nym asks him whether he is a Child of the Dragon.   

{{quote|Jonai winced. That name had caused trouble, no less for not being true. But how many citizens now believed the Da'shain Aiel had once served the Dragon and no other Aes Sedai?{{ref/book|4|26}}}}

== Third reference ==
{{quote|And when the blood was sprinkled on ground where nothing could grow, the Children of the Dragon did spring up, the People of the Dragon, armed to dance with death. And he did call them forth from the wasted lands, and they did shake the world with battle.|The Wheel of Time by [[Sulamein so Bhagad]] Chief Historian at the Court of the Sun, the Fourth Age{{ref/book|4|58}}}}
